title: Premier League model recap — 2026-08-22
summary: The model went 1/5 (20%) on graded Premier League picks.
body: Matchday's model graded 5 Premier League picks this stretch, hitting on 1 of them (20%). Over the same 5 games with a market line, the betting market favorite hit 40% of the time.
On calibration: picks stated at <50% hit 33% of the time (3 games). A well-calibrated model's stated confidence should roughly match its actual hit rate in each band.

Among this week's Premier League storylines: the biggest upset was Leeds United FC winning 0-1 against Nottingham Forest FC (the market gave that result only about 32%); the model's best call was Everton FC in Everton FC vs Crystal Palace FC at 44% confidence; its biggest miss was picking Manchester United FC in Hull City AFC vs Manchester United FC, but Hull City AFC won instead.

This is Matchday's own model reporting on itself for anyone to use. Every pick is locked before kickoff and graded automatically once the game finishes; none are rewritten after the fact. See the Q&A page for how the model works.

title: MLB model recap — 2026-08-21
summary: The model went 136/263 (52%) on graded MLB picks.
body: Matchday's model graded 263 MLB picks this stretch, hitting on 136 of them (52%). Over the same 158 games with a market line, the betting market favorite hit 52% of the time.

On calibration: picks stated at 50-60% hit 50% of the time (124 games); picks stated at 60-70% hit 52% of the time (86 games); picks stated at 70-80% hit 56% of the time (43 games); picks stated at 80-90% hit 50% of the time (10 games). A well-calibrated model's stated confidence should roughly match its actual hit rate in each band.

The strongest signal lately has been opponent-adjusted rating: when it favored a side, that side won 56% of the time (125 games). Championship market power has been the weakest, at 17% (12 games) — a reminder no single factor is decisive on its own.

Among this week's MLB storylines: the biggest upset was San Diego Padres winning 5-7 against Cleveland Guardians (the market gave that result only about 48%); the model's best call was San Diego Padres in Cleveland Guardians vs San Diego Padres at 59% confidence; its biggest miss was picking Chicago Cubs in Chicago Cubs vs St. Louis Cardinals, but St. Louis Cardinals won instead.

This is Matchday's own model reporting on itself for anyone to use. Every pick is locked before kickoff and graded automatically once the game finishes; none are rewritten after the fact. See the Q&A page for how the model works.

title: Hypothetical Matchup: Bills vs. Lions, Under a Closed Roof
summary: A transparent neutral-site simulation of two 2025 team profiles — clearly not a forecast or real fixture.
body: A fictional neutral-site game between the 2025 Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions profiles produces a 55.1% to 44.9% simulated split.
The scenario freezes 2025 team-era inputs, uses equal rest and a roofed neutral venue, and makes no present-day roster, injury, market, or fixture claim.
Sensitivity cases show that home field or small changes to the passing and explosive-play assumptions can reverse or sharply narrow the result.
